interfaceDesign: No new public surface — tests/e2e/testdata/repo/.gitignore is a static fixture file, and TestSetUpProjectCommitsTheFixturesGitignore is a package-internal test calling the existing unexported setUpProject and run helpers.

selfReview.item: Every public method has an intention-revealing name (no process/handle/manage)
Cyclomatic complexity < 7 on all new functions
selfReview.note: golangci-lint run ./tests/e2e/... reported 0 issues; the new test has three sequential error checks, no branching logic.

selfReview.item: No primitive obsession: domain concepts wrapped in value objects, not raw strings/ints
selfReview.note: Not applicable — a static .gitignore fixture and a test calling existing typed helpers.

selfReview.item: No feature envy: methods use their own class's data more than another's
No magic numbers or strings: all literals are named constants
selfReview.note: The .gitignore paths and order id 'x' are inherent to the fixture/test, not business-logic literals.

selfReview.item: Dependency direction verified: nothing in inner layers imports from outer layers
selfReview.note: No internal/ or cmd/ files touched; test only calls existing tests/e2e/harness package functions.

simpleDesign.note: go test ./tests/e2e/... — all tests pass, including TestTheFactoryDeliversTheFixtureOrder (every check PASS) and TestTheHarnessFailsARunThatDeliversTheWrongThing (still fails only its two expected checks).
TestSetUpProjectCommitsTheFixturesGitignore names exactly what it proves; the fixture .gitignore mirrors the root .gitignore's own comments for its two entries.
Test reuses the existing fixture(), run(), and setUpProject() helpers rather than reimplementing git plumbing.
One new file, one new test function, no changes to deliver.go or exec.go — confirmed by inspection that copyTree already copies dotfiles unfiltered.

keyDecisions.decision: Scoped the fixture's .gitignore to only the two per-machine entries (.claude/feature-workspace/, .claude/memory/) rather than mirroring the full root .gitignore.
keyDecisions.reasoning: The spec and analysis both call for only these two per-machine run-state entries; the fixture has no .env, .loom/, or other paths of its own that the rest of the root .gitignore excludes, so copying more would be dead weight.

keyDecisions.decision: Wrote the new test against setUpProject directly (not the full Deliver/Run path) and read the commit back via `git show HEAD:.gitignore` using the package's existing run() helper.
keyDecisions.reasoning: setUpProject is exactly the step that copies the fixture tree and makes the project's first commit; calling it directly keeps the test fast and isolates the behaviour the acceptance criterion is about, without needing a factory pass.

keyDecisions.decision: Made no changes to deliver.go or exec.go.
keyDecisions.reasoning: copyTree (exec.go) walks the fixture with filepath.WalkDir and no name filtering, and setUpProject's existing `git add -A` already stages dotfiles — verified by the new test passing without any change to either file, resolving the spec's Open Question.

notesForQa: go test ./tests/e2e/... passes end to end with the mock provider: TestTheFactoryDeliversTheFixtureOrder prints PASS for every check (including the pre-existing ones), and TestTheHarnessFailsARunThatDeliversTheWrongThing still fails only 'the diff stays inside scope.paths' and 'the hidden acceptance tests pass'.

The new TestSetUpProjectCommitsTheFixturesGitignore in tests/e2e/harness/units_test.go asserts byte-for-byte equality between tests/e2e/testdata/repo/.gitignore and the file read back via `git show HEAD:.gitignore` in the project worktree setUpProject creates.
